==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/pɑːs/}} ** {{IPA|en|[pʰɑːs]|a=RP,South Africa}} ** {{IPA|en|[pʰäːs]|[pʰɐːs]|a=AU,NZ}} ** {{IPA|en|[pʰaːs]|a=Boston}} * {{IPA|en|/pæs/}} ** {{IPA|en|[pʰæs]|[pʰɛə̯s]|[pʰeə̯s]|a=GA,Canada}} * {{audio|en|en-us-pass.ogg|a=US}} ** {{IPA|en|[pʰas]|[pʰæs]|a=Ireland,Northern England}} ** {{IPA|en|[pʰäs]|a=Scotland}} ** {{IPA|en|[pʰeə̯s]|a=NYC}} * {{rhymes|en|æs|ɑːs|s=1}} * {{hyphenation|en|pass}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|id=verb|:inh|enm:passen|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|passen}}, from {{der|en|fro|passer||to step, walk, pass}}, from {{der|en|la-vul|*passo|*passāre|t=step, walk, pass}}, derived from {{der|en|la|passus||a step}}, from {{der|en|itc-pro|*pattus|*pat-s-tus}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*peth₂-||to spread, stretch out}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|fæþm||armful, fathom}}. More at {{l|en|fathom}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|genġan}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|passe||obsolete}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # ''To [[change]] [[place]].'' ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To move or be moved from one place to another. ##: {{syn|en|go|move}} ##: {{ux|en|They '''passed''' from room to room.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To go past, by, over, or through; to proceed from one side to the other of; to move [[past]]. ##: {{syn|en|overtake|pass by|pass over}} ##: {{ux|en|You will '''pass''' a house on your right.}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=We expressed our readiness, and in ten minutes were in the station wagon, rolling rapidly down the long drive, for it was then after nine. We '''passed''' on the way the van of the guests from Asquith.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1944|author={{w|Cecil Street|Miles Burton}} |title=[https://openlibrary.org/works/OL10563347W The Three Corpse Trick]|chapter=5 |passage=The dinghy was trailing astern at the end of its painter, and Merrion looked at it as he '''passed'''. He saw that it was a battered-looking affair of the prahm type, with a blunt snout, and like the parent ship, had recently been painted a vivid green.}} ## {{senseid|en|transfer}}{{lb|en|ditransitive}} To cause to move or go; to [[send]]; to [[transfer]] from one person, place, or condition to another. ##: {{syn|en|deliver|give|hand|make over|send|transfer|transmit|pass off}} ##: {{ux|en|The waiter '''passed''' biscuits and cheese.}} ##: {{ux|en|John '''passed''' Suzie a note.}} ##: {{ux|en|The torch was '''passed''' from hand to hand.}} ##* {{RQ:Addison Italy |passage=I had only time to '''pass''' my eye over the medals.}} ##* {{RQ:Clarendon History|passage=Waller {{...}} '''passed''' over five thousand horse and foot by Newbridge.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|transitive|medicine}} To eliminate (something) from the body by natural processes. ##: {{syn|en|evacuate|void}} ##: {{ux|en|He was '''passing''' blood in both his urine and his stool.}} ##: {{ux|en|The poison had been '''passed''' by the time of the autopsy.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|nautical}} To take a turn with (a line, gasket, etc.), as around a sail in furling, and make secure. ## {{lb|en|sport}} {{n-g|To make various kinds of movement.}} ### {{lb|en|transitive|football}} To kick (the ball) with precision rather than at full force. ### {{senseid|en|to teammate}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To move (the ball or puck) to a [[teammate]]. ###* {{quote-journal|en|date=September 18, 2017|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4E1dDwAAQBAJ|journal=Boston Globe|author=Nicole Yang|title=What you need to know about the Patriots’ big win — and their next opponent|passage=Brady '''passed''' the ball to nine different receivers and handed it off to seven.}} ### {{lb|en|intransitive|fencing}} To make a lunge or swipe. ###: {{syn|en|thrust}} ### {{lb|en|intransitive|American football}} To throw the ball, generally [[downfield]], towards a teammate. ###: {{ux|en|The Patriots '''passed''' on third and long.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To go from one person to another. ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To put in circulation; to give currency to. ##: {{syn|en|circulate|pass around}} ##: {{ux|en|'''pass''' counterfeit money}} ## {{lbl|en|transitive}} To cause to obtain entrance, admission, or conveyance. ##: {{syn|en|admit|let in|[[let]] [[past]]}} ##: {{ux|en|'''pass''' a person into a theater or over a railroad}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|culinary}} To put through a [[sieve]]. ##: {{ux|en|When it's finished cooking, you should '''pass''' the sauce to get rid of any lumps.}} # ''To change in state or status'' ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[progress]] from one state to another; to [[advance]]. ##: {{ux|en|He '''passed''' from youth into old age.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[depart]], to [[cease]], to come to an [[end]]. ##: {{ux|en|At first, she was worried, but that feeling soon '''passed'''.}} ##* {{RQ:Dryden Virgil|Pastoral 2 |passage=Beauty's a charm, but soon the charm will '''pass'''.}} ##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=23|passage=The slightest effort made the patient cough. He would stand leaning on a stick and holding a hand to his side, and when the paroxysm had '''passed''' it left him shaking.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1995|author=Penny Richards|title=The Greatest Gift of All |passage=The crisis '''passed''' as she'd prayed it would, but it remained to be seen just how much damage had been done.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|euphemism}} To [[die]]. ##: {{syn|en|pass away|pass on|pass over|Thesaurus:die}} ##: {{ux|en|His grandmother '''passed''' yesterday.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|transitive}} To achieve a [[successful]] outcome from. ##: {{ux|en|He attempted the examination, but did not expect to '''pass'''.}} ##: {{ux|en|Of the Ancient Wonders, only the pyramids have '''passed''' the test of time.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|transitive}} To advance through all the steps or stages necessary to become [[valid]] or [[effective]]; to obtain the formal sanction of (a legislative body). ##: {{syn|en|be [[accept]]ed by}} ##: {{ux|en|Despite the efforts of the opposition, the bill '''passed'''.}} ##: {{ux|en|The bill '''passed''' both houses of Congress.}} ##: {{ux|en|The bill '''passed''' the Senate, but did not '''pass''' in the House.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|date=2012-03|author=William E. Carter; Merri Sue Carter |volume=100|issue=2|page=87|magazine=w:American Scientist |title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/the-british-longitude-act-reconsidered The British Longitude Act Reconsidered] |passage=But was it responsible governance to '''pass''' the Longitude Act without other efforts to protect British seamen? Or might it have been subterfuge—a disingenuous attempt to shift attention away from the realities of their life at sea.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|author=w:CalMatters|title=How Airbnb is fighting for its place on California's coast|journal=w:San Francisco Chronicle|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260928044005/https://www.sfchronicle.com/bayarea/article/airbnb-fighting-on-california-s-coast-in-bay-22450830.php|date=27 September 2026 |passage=Officials in Pacifica recently tried to '''pass''' rules aimed at curtailing short-term vacation rentals, only to meet unexpected stiff resistance.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|legal}} To be conveyed or transferred by will, deed, or other instrument of conveyance. ##: {{ux|en|The estate '''passes''' by the third clause in Mr Smith's deed to his son.}} ##: {{ux|en|When the old king passed away with only a daughter as an heir, the throne '''passed''' to a woman for the first time in centuries.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause to advance by stages of progress; to carry on with success through an ordeal, examination, or action; specifically, to give legal or official sanction to; to ratify; to enact; to approve as valid and just. ##: {{syn|en|approve|enact|ratify}} ##: {{ux|en|He '''passed''' the bill through the committee.}} ##* {{RQ:Tennyson Maud|passage='''Pass''' the happy news.}} ## {{senseid|en|judge}} {{lb|en|intransitive|legal}} To make a [[judgment]] ''on'' or ''upon'' a person or case. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1485|author=Sir {{w|Thomas Malory}}|title=w:Le Morte d'Arthur|section=Book X |passage=And within three dayes twelve knyghtes '''passed''' uppon hem; and they founde Sir Palomydes gylty, and Sir Saphir nat gylty, of the lordis deth.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To utter; to pronounce; to pledge. ##: {{syn|en|pronounce|say|speak|utter}} ##* {{RQ:Fielding Tom Jones|book=XIX|chapter=XII|passage=I may almost depend on your own justice, and leave it to yourself to pass sentence on your own conduct}} ##* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|text=Father, thy word is '''passed'''.|year=1873}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To change from one state to another (without the implication of progression). # ''To move through time.'' ## {{lb|en|intransitive|of time}} To [[elapse]], to be spent. ##: {{syn|en|elapse|go by|Thesaurus:elapse}} ##: {{ux|en|Their vacation '''passed''' pleasantly.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|of time}} To [[spend]]. ##: {{ux|en|What will we do to '''pass''' the time?}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1667|author=w:John Milton|title=Paradise Lost |passage=To '''pass''' commodiously this life.}} ##* {{RQ:Belloc Lowndes Lodger|I|0056|passage=Thanks to that penny he had just spent so recklessly [on a newspaper] he would '''pass''' a happy hour, taken, for once, out of his anxious, despondent, miserable self. It irritated him shrewdly to know that these moments of respite from carking care would not be shared with his poor wife, with careworn, troubled Ellen.}} ##* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=23|passage=For, although Allan had '''passed''' his fiftieth year,{{...}}, one had continued to think of him as a man of whipcord and iron, a natural source of untiring energy, a mechanism that would not wear out.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To allow to go by without noticing; to omit attention to; to take no note of; to disregard. ##: {{syn|en|disregard|ignore|take no notice of|Thesaurus:ignore}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Coriolanus|II|ii|passage=Please you that I may '''pass''' / This doing.}} ##* {{RQ:Dryden Fables|chapter=Palamon and Arcite|passage=I '''pass''' their warlike pomp, their proud array.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To continue. ##: {{syn|en|continue|go on}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To proceed without hindrance or opposition. ##: {{ux|en|You're late, but I'll let it '''pass'''.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To live through; to have experience of; to undergo; to suffer. ##: {{syn|en|bear|endure|suffer|tolerate|undergo|Thesaurus:tolerate}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Othello|I|iii|passage=Please you that I may '''pass''' / This doing.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[happen]]. ##: {{syn|en|happen|occur|Thesaurus:happen}} ##: {{ux|en|It will soon come to '''pass'''.}} ##*: {{...}}for the memory of what '''passed''' while at that place is almost blank. # ''To be accepted.'' ## {{lb|en|intransitive|stative}} To be [[tolerate]]d as a substitute for something else, to "[[do]]". ##: {{ux|en|It isn't ideal, but it will '''pass'''.}} ## {{senseid|en|sociology}} {{lb|en|intransitive|stative|sociology}} To be accepted by others as a member of a [[race]], [[sex]]{{,}} or other [[group]] to which one does not belong or would not have originally appeared to belong; especially to be considered [[white]] although one has [[black]] [[ancestry]], or a [[woman]] although one was [[assign]]ed [[male]] at birth or [[vice versa]]. ##: {{cot|en|roleplay|gloss=act out a social role}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|date=1941 December 22|title=How to Tell Japs from the Chinese|journal={{w|Life (magazine)|LIFE}}|trans-journal=|issue=|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y04EAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA81|page=81|passage=Chinese sometimes '''pass''' for Europeans, but Japs more often approach Western types.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1999|author=Irene Preiss|title=Fixed for Life: The True Saga of How Tom Became Sally|page=249|passage={{...}} a situation where I had to know whether I could '''pass''' as a woman, and not tell anyone, and not be asked what I was doing dressed as a woman.}} # ''To refrain from doing something.'' ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To decline something that is offered or available. ##: {{cot|en|pass on|pass up}} ##: {{ux|en|He asked me to go to the cinema with him, but I think I'll '''pass'''.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To reject; to [[pass up]]. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=Joshua D. Wolff|title=Western Union and the Creation of the American Corporate Order, 1845-1893|page=187 |passage=Instead, the board voted to suspend the dividend, giving Orton his way at last. They '''passed''' the dividend again in June 1870 {{...}}}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To decline or not attempt to answer a question. ##: {{ux|en|I haven't any idea of the answer, so I'll have to '''pass'''.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} In turn-based games, to decline to play in one's turn. ## {{lb|en|intransitive|card games}} In [[euchre]], to decline to make the trump. # ''To do or be better.'' ## {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To go beyond bounds; to surpass; to be in excess. ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|IV|ii|passage=This '''passes''', Master Ford.}} ##: {{syn|en|exceed|surpass}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To transcend; to surpass; to excel; to exceed. ##: {{syn|en|better|exceed|excel|outdo|surpass|transcend|Thesaurus:exceed}} ##* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=II|canto=VI|stanza=25|passage=And striue to '''passe'''{{...}}Their natiue musicke by her skilfull art:}} ##* {{RQ:Byron Childe Harold|canto=C|passage=Whose tender power '''Passes''' the strength of storms in their most desolate hour.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[take heed]], to have an [[interest]], to [[care]]. #: {{syn|en|take heed|take notice|Thesaurus:pay attention}} #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=i|page=18|passage=''Mena[phon].'' How now my Lord, what mated and amazd’
To heare the king thus threaten like himſelfe?
''Coſ[roe].'' Ah Menaphon, I '''paſſe''' not for his threates, {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 6-2|act=IV|scene=ii|passage=As for these silken-coated slaves, I '''pass''' not.}} =====Conjugation===== {{m|enm|pase}}, {{m|enm|pace}}, from {{m|enm|passen||to pass}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # An [[opening]], road, or track, available for passing; especially, one through or over some dangerous or otherwise impracticable barrier such as a mountain range; a [[passageway]]; a defile; a ford. #: {{synonyms|en|gap|notch}} #: {{ux|en|[[mountain pass|mountain '''pass''']]}} #* {{RQ:Longfellow Ballads|poem=Excelsior|stanza=4|page=130|passage="Try not the '''Pass'''!" the old man said; / "Dark lowers the tempest overhead, / The roaring torrent is deep and wide!" / And loud that clarion voice replied / Excelsior!}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1910|first=Maud|last=Diver|authorlink=Maud Diver|chapter=The Valley of Decision|title=The Great Amulet |url=https://archive.org/details/greatamulet00divegoog/|location=New York|publisher=w:John Lane Company|OCLC=7035847|page=368 |pageurl=https://archive.org/details/greatamulet00divegoog/page/n380/|text=Followed two more weeks of marching,—rougher marching this time,—through the core of the lofty mountains that divide India
